words.gloss: peacock (śikhin); cock (kukkuṭa); swan or goose (haṃsa); egg (aṇḍa); arising from, produced from

hindi: तेल और घी, जो मोर, मुर्गे और हंस के अण्डों से उत्पन्न हों।
english: Oil and ghee (taila and sarpis), arising from the eggs of the peacock, the cock and the swan,
notes: Elliptical: no verb in this unit (the governing verb stands outside this chunk); none supplied. 'saṃbhavam' is singular neuter while 'tailasarpiṣī' is dual, so the agreement is loose; the Sanskrit does not say whether the oil and ghee come from the eggs or are prepared with them, so the literal 'arising from' is kept. 'śikhin' is taken as peacock (it can also mean other crested things). 'haṃsa' = swan or goose (waterbird).

words.gloss: dhātrī (emblic myrobalan, Phyllanthus emblica; standard); vidārī (probably Pueraria tuberosa; probable); expressed juice (svarasa)
of the cow (gavya); milk (kṣīra); āḍhaka (a measure of volume); a pair, two

hindi: धात्री यानी आँवला और विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द का स्वरस, और गाय के दूध के दो आढक।
english: The expressed juice (svarasa) of dhātrī (emblic myrobalan) and of vidārī (probably Pueraria tuberosa), and two āḍhakas of cow's milk,
notes: Identifications: dhātrī = āmalakī, Phyllanthus emblica (standard); vidārī = Pueraria tuberosa, vidārīkanda (probable; Ipomoea digitata is sometimes given). The āḍhaka is a measure of volume. Still a list of ingredients; no verb here.

words.gloss: brahma (uncertain sense here); bherī (kettledrum); mṛdaṅga (a drum)

hindi: और जो ब्रह्म, भेरी और मृदंग की ध्वनियों से तैयार किया गया हो।
english: And that which is prepared with the sounds of brahma, bherī (kettledrum) and mṛdaṅga (drum),
notes: The sense of 'brahma' at the start of the compound is not sure: it may be a sound (sacred recitation) or part of a drum name; it is kept as 'brahma' and not enriched. bherī = kettledrum, mṛdaṅga = a drum (both standard). The thing prepared is not named in this unit (neuter, 'yat').

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. ava-√guṇṭh, n. nom. sg.

hindi: जिस पर श्वेत छत्र से छाया की गई हो और जो श्वेत वस्त्र से ढका हो।
english: Shaded by a white umbrella, covered with a white cloth,
notes: Describes the prepared substance (neuter, understood from the previous unit); no noun is stated here, so none is added. 'sitacchatra' is sita-chatra with doubled c.

words.gram: ppp. caus. ā-√ruh, n. nom. sg.

words.gloss: Vṛṣadhvaja (the bull-bannered one, an epithet of Śiva; standard)

hindi: हाथी के कन्धे पर रखा हुआ, वृषध्वज यानी शिव की पूजा करके।
english: Placed on the shoulder of an elephant, having worshipped Vṛṣadhvaja (the bull-bannered one, Śiva),
notes: 'vṛṣadhvaja' literally 'having a bull as banner'; it is the usual epithet of Śiva (standard), which the line itself does not state. The agent of the worship is not named. 'skandha' = shoulder or back.

hindi: स्वस्त्ययन करके बिना नियन्त्रण के स्नेहबस्ति दे।
english: Having performed the svastyayana (auspicious rite), one should give a sneha-basti (unctuous enema) without restriction.
notes: 'ayantraṇam' is neuter while 'basti' is masculine, so it is read as an adverb 'without restriction'; what is left unrestricted (diet, conduct) is not stated. The giver is unnamed.

hindi: उससे अत्यधिक वृषता पाकर वह सौ स्त्रियों को थका दे।
english: Having obtained excessive virility by that, he would exhaust a hundred women.

text_flags.why: possible: 'prāptes' is not a form that fits; 'prāptaḥ' (prāptas before t) gives the nominative 'having obtained' that the sentence needs
possible: 'dhanitā' is not a word; 'vanitā' (woman) fits the sense; the printed 'ddh' may come from d+v misread

notes: Two doubtful spots (see text_flags). 'ativṛṣatā' = excess of vṛṣatā (virility, from vṛṣa 'bull, potent'). The optative 'would exhaust' is literal; the agent 'he' is not stated.

hindi: वह झुर्रियों और सफेद बालों से रहित, कान्त और चिरंजीवी हो जाएगा।
english: And he would become free of wrinkles and grey hair, handsome and long-lived.

text_flags.why: possible: 'pulita' is not a word; 'palita' (grey hair) is the usual pair with 'valī' (wrinkles)

notes: 'kānta' = pleasing, handsome, beloved; the more literal 'handsome' is used. 'valī' = skin fold, wrinkle.

words.gloss: lost; semen (śukra) — one whose semen is lost
irregular fever (viṣamajvara; intermittent fever, probable) — those having it

hindi: जिनका शुक्र नष्ट हो गया है, जो क्षत हैं, क्षीण हैं और विषमज्वर वाले हैं, उनके लिए हितकर।
english: Beneficial for those whose semen (śukra) is lost, who are injured, who are wasted, and who have irregular fever (viṣamajvara).
notes: Identification: viṣamajvara = irregular or intermittent fever (probable; the group of fevers returning at intervals). 'kṣata-kṣīṇa' could also be read as one compound 'wasted through injury'; they are taken here as two separate members. The subject ('it') is not stated. 'naṣṭaśukra' is taken as 'one whose semen is lost'.

words.gloss: spoiled, disordered; menstrual blood (ārtava); semen (śukra) — of those in whom these are spoiled

hindi: जिनका आर्तव और शुक्र बिगड़ गया है, उनके लिए पुत्र देने वाला और रसायन।
english: For those whose menstrual blood (ārtava) and semen (śukra) are spoiled, a giver of sons and a rasāyana (rejuvenating tonic).

text_flags.why: the printed 'śuqāṇām' (ka with a dot, no ra) is not a word; 'śukrāṇām' (gen. pl. of śukra) is clearly meant, and 'ārttava' is printed for ārtava

notes: Elliptical (no verb, subject 'it' understood). 'rasāyana' is kept with a short gloss; it names the branch of rejuvenation, and here a rejuvenating remedy. Normalisation: doubled -rtt- written -rt- in 'ārtava'.

words.gloss: to be devised, to be prepared

hindi: और इस प्रकार अन्य बस्तियाँ भी बनाई जानी चाहिए और अनेक प्रकार से पकाई जानी चाहिए।
english: And in this way other bastis (enemas) also are to be devised, and are to be cooked, in many ways.
notes: 'naikaśaḥ' = na + ekaśaḥ, literally 'not singly', i.e. in many ways. 'basti' here is the enema.

hindi: सम्भव होने पर सौ बार या हजार बार पकवाए।
english: One should have it cooked a hundred times or a thousand, when it is possible.
notes: 'saṃbhave sati' is a locative absolute, 'there being possibility'. 'sahasram' is read with 'vārān' (a thousand times). The object (what is cooked) is not stated; the causative 'pācayet' is rendered 'should have cooked'.

hindi: दोषों का नाश करने वाली स्नेहबस्तियाँ, परिहार सहित, कही जाएँगी।
english: Sneha-bastis (unctuous enemas) that destroy the doṣas will be described, together with their precautions (parīhāra).
notes: 'parīhāra' = avoidance, precaution (things to avoid). 'vakṣyante' is the passive future, 'will be told'.

words.gloss: the group of ten roots (daśamūla; standard)

hindi: दशमूल यानी दस जड़ों का समूह, वरा यानी सम्भवतः त्रिफला, रास्ना यानी सम्भवतः रासन, अश्वगन्धा यानी असगन्ध और पुनर्नवा यानी गदहपूरना।
english: The daśamūla (the group of ten roots), varā (probably triphalā), rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata), aśvagandhā (ashwagandha, Withania somnifera) and punarnavā (Boerhavia diffusa),
notes: Ingredient list (accusative); the verb is not in this unit. Identifications: daśamūla = the traditional group of ten roots, usually bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, pāṭalā, gambhārī, śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura (standard; the line itself does not list them); varā = triphalā in the nighaṇṭus (probable); rāsnā = Pluchea lanceolata (disputed; Alpinia galanga and orchids are also given); aśvagandhā = Withania somnifera (standard); punarnavā = Boerhavia diffusa (standard).

words.gloss: bhūtīka (disputed; sometimes a fragrant grass, not enriched here)

hindi: गुडूची यानी गिलोय, एरण्ड यानी अरंडी, भूतीक, भार्गी यानी भारंगी, वृषक यानी सम्भवतः अडूसा और शिरीष।
english: Guḍūcī (giloy), eraṇḍa (castor), bhūtīka, bhārgī (Clerodendrum serratum), vṛṣaka (probably Justicia adhatoda) and śirīṣa (Albizia lebbeck),

text_flags.why: possible: the extra anusvāra in 'ṃraṃḍa' looks like a slip (guḍūcy-airaṇḍa or guḍūcy-eraṇḍa); 'śeriṣa' is not a known plant name and 'śirīṣa' fits

notes: One long compound (dvandva) of drug names, accusative. Identifications: guḍūcī = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); eraṇḍa/airaṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard); bhūtīka = disputed (a fragrant grass such as bhūstṛṇa is often given), so no firm identification; bhārgī = Clerodendrum serratum (standard); vṛṣaka = vāsaka, Justicia adhatoda (probable); śirīṣa = Albizia lebbeck (standard). The split of 'guḍūcyaiṃraṃḍa…' is uncertain.

words.gloss: sahacara (probably Barleria prionitis; probable, colour varieties differ)

hindi: शतावरी, सहचर यानी सम्भवतः कटसरैया, काकनासा और जिसका भाग एक पल है।
english: Śatāvarī (Asparagus racemosus), sahacara (probably Barleria), kākanāsā, and (the one) having a pala as share.
notes: Identifications: śatāvarī = Asparagus racemosus (standard); sahacara = Barleria prionitis (probable; other Barleria species, differing in flower colour, are also called sahacara); kākanāsā = disputed (several plants proposed), so only the name is kept. 'palāṃśika' = 'having a pala as share'; the noun it qualifies is not stated, and 'each' is not in the Sanskrit; it may qualify the whole list. The printed 'ḻ' (paḻa) is written 'l' (pala) in the split (orthographic normalisation, recorded here once).

words.gloss: kola (probably jujube berry, Ziziphus jujuba; probable)

hindi: यव, माष यानी उड़द, अतसी यानी अलसी, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी, प्रसृत से मापे हुए।
english: Yava (barley), māṣa (black gram), atasī (flax), kola (probably jujube berries) and kulattha (horse gram), measured by prasṛta.
notes: Dvandva of five items, accusative plural. Identifications: yava = barley (standard); māṣa = Vigna mungo (standard); atasī = Linum usitatissimum (standard); kola = Ziziphus jujuba, the jujube berry (probable; kola is also a name of other things); kulattha = Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard). 'prasṛta' is a measure, the amount held in a cupped palm; 'each' is not in the Sanskrit.

hindi: वह नामक माप के जल में पकाकर, एक द्रोण शेष रहने पर, और उससे भी।
english: Having boiled (it) in a vaha of water, with a droṇa remaining, and with that.
notes: Doubtful sense of 'vahe': taken as the measure vaha ('a vaha of water'), with the genitive 'toyasya'. The size of the vaha and droṇa is not worked out here. 'droṇaśeṣeṇa' = 'with a droṇa as remainder', i.e. boiled down until a droṇa is left. 'tena' (with that) refers to the resulting liquid, continued in the next unit; the object being boiled is not stated.

hindi: एक आढक तेल को पीसने योग्य, जीवनीय, पल से मापे हुओं के साथ पकाए।
english: One should cook an āḍhaka of oil with (ones) to be ground, the life-promoting (jīvanīya) (ones), measured by a pala.
notes: The nouns are not stated, so '(ones)' is used. 'jīvanīya' is the traditional group of ten drugs (standard): jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka; the line itself does not list them. 'with that' of the previous unit (the decoction) continues here; no verb is supplied beyond 'pacet'.

words.gloss: all; Vāta; disorder; dispelling (final d written t)

hindi: यह अनुवासन कहलाता है, सब वातविकारों को दूर करने वाला।
english: This, called anuvāsana (unctuous retention enema), dispels all disorders of Vāta.
notes: Name given in the line: 'anuvāsana'. 'anuvāsana' is the oil enema retained for a time (standard). The stem of the last member is -nud, shown as -nut by the final devoicing in print.

words.gloss: of marsh-dwelling (ones), animals of marshy ground

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. upa-√sādh, f. nom. sg.

hindi: अनूप जीवों की वसा, उसी प्रकार जीवनीयों से तैयार की गई।
english: The fat (vasā) of the marsh-dwelling (ones), prepared similarly with the jīvanīya (ones).
notes: Elliptical, no verb. 'ānūpa' = belonging to marshy (watery) country; the noun (animals) is not stated, so '(ones)'. 'jīvanīya' see unit 97. 'tadvat' refers to the preparation of the previous unit.

hindi: शताह्वा यानी सोआ, यव, बिल्व यानी बेल और खट्टों से सिद्ध किया तेल, समीरण यानी वात में।
english: Oil cooked with śatāhvā (dill), yava (barley), bilva (bael) and sour (ones), for wind (samīraṇa, that is Vāta).
notes: Print convention: 'śatāvhā' is the printed form of śatāhvā (recorded here once for this and later units). 'amla' is read as 'sour (ones)' (unstated nouns); the sense could also be a single sour drug. 'samīraṇa' = wind, a name for Vāta (standard); the locative is read 'for/against wind'. Identifications: śatāhvā = Anethum sowa (standard); bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard).

hindi: सेंधा नमक से, जो अग्नि के रंग का हो, तपाया गया और वात को जीतने वाला घी।
english: Ghee (ghṛta), heated with rock salt (saindhava) of fire colour, and conquering Vāta.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhṛtam' (held) gives no good sense after 'taptam'; 'ghṛtam' (ghee) fits the context of oils and ghees and the metre

notes: The reading 'ghee' rests on the suggested correction (see text_flags); on the printed 'dhṛta' the sense would be 'held/kept'. 'agnivarṇa' = fire-coloured, i.e. red-hot or glowing; the line does not say how the salt is used beyond 'heated with'. 'anilajit' = conquering Vāta (anila = wind).

words.gloss: medā (disputed; one of the aṣṭavarga drugs, not enriched)

hindi: जीवन्ती, मदन यानी मैनफल, मेदा, श्रावणी यानी सम्भवतः गोरखमुण्डी, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और बला यानी बरियार।
english: Jīvantī, madana (emetic nut), medā, śrāvaṇī (probably Sphaeranthus indicus), madhuka (probably liquorice) and balā (Sida cordifolia),
notes: Ingredient list. Identifications: jīvantī = Leptadenia reticulata (standard); madana = Randia dumetorum (standard); medā = disputed (a tuber of the aṣṭavarga group, often replaced; no firm botanical name); śrāvaṇī = Sphaeranthus indicus (probable); madhuka = Glycyrrhiza glabra (probable; Madhuca longifolia is also called madhuka); balā = Sida cordifolia (standard). The printed 'ḻ' (baḻā) is written 'l'.

words.gloss: śatāhvā (dill; see unit 100); ṛṣabhaka (a drug of the aṣṭavarga group; disputed, not enriched)

hindi: शताह्वा यानी सोआ और ऋषभक, कृष्णा यानी सम्भवतः पिप्पली, काकनासा और शतावरी।
english: Śatāhvā (dill) and ṛṣabhaka, kṛṣṇā (probably pippalī, long pepper), kākanāsā and śatāvarī,
notes: 'śatāvharṣabhakau' is read as śatāhva + ṛṣabhaka in a dual dvandva (a + ṛ = ar); the stem shows the short final -a as compound member. 'kṛṣṇā' (lit. black) is taken as pippalī, Piper longum (probable; the word has other meanings).

words.gloss: śaṭhī (probably Hedychium spicatum; probable, Curcuma zedoaria also given)

hindi: स्वगुप्ता यानी कौंच, क्षीरकाकोली, कर्कट नामक, शठी यानी सम्भवतः कपूरकचरी और वचा यानी बच।
english: Svaguptā (cowhage), kṣīrakākolī, (that) named karkaṭa, śaṭhī (probably Hedychium spicatum) and vacā (sweet flag),
notes: 'karkaṭākhyā' = 'named karkaṭa' (crab); the drug usually meant is karkaṭaśṛṅgī, Pistacia integerrima galls (probable), but the line only says 'named karkaṭa'. kṣīrakākolī: disputed (Roscoea or Lilium species proposed). svaguptā = ātmaguptā, Mucuna pruriens (standard). vacā = Acorus calamus (standard).

hindi: पीसकर तेल और घी को चौगुने दूध में पकाए।
english: Having ground (them), one should cook oil (and) ghee in fourfold milk.

text_flags.why: possible: the instrumental plural does not agree with 'kṣīre' (locative singular); the parallel line 'kṣīre caturguṇe' in the next unit but two suggests 'caturguṇe'

notes: Translation follows the suggested 'caturguṇe' (fourfold, in relation to the oil and ghee is not stated). On the printed instrumental plural the sense would be 'with fourfold (ones)'. 'tailam ghṛtam' read as two objects; the ground substances are not named in this unit.

words.gloss: strength; semen; fire (agni, the digestive fire); increasing

hindi: पोषण करने वाला, वात और पित्त का नाश करने वाला, बल, शुक्र और अग्नि को बढ़ाने वाला।
english: Nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa), destroying Vāta and Pitta, increasing strength, semen (śukra) and the fire (agni, the digestive fire).
notes: Elliptical (no verb). Orthographic: printed 'varddhana' written vardhana. 'agni' = the digestive fire, as is usual in such lists; the line says only 'fire'.

hindi: रज और शुक्र के रोगों को दूर करने वाला, और पुत्रीय अनुवासन।
english: Removing ailments of menstrual blood (rajas) and semen (śukra), and the putrīya (son-related) anuvāsana.
notes: 'putrīya' = 'relating to/for a son'; it seems to be a name of this anuvāsana, but the line does not say how it is meant, so it is kept literal. 'raja(s)' is taken as menstrual blood here (standard in this setting). Elliptical, no verb.

words.gloss: cold; touch; potency (vīrya) — (ones) of cold touch and potency

hindi: शीतल स्पर्श और वीर्य वालों से, और पिसे हुओं से, चौगुने दूध में।
english: And with (ones) of cold touch and potency (vīrya), ground, in fourfold milk.
notes: Unstated nouns (drugs) are shown as '(ones)'. 'śiśira-sparśa-vīrya' can be read 'cold in touch and in potency' or 'having cold touch and (cold) potency'; 'śiśira' is taken with both. No verb in this unit.

words.gloss: oil; quarter — having oil as a quarter

hindi: तेल को चौथाई भाग रखकर पकाया गया घी, पित्त का नाश करने वाला अनुवासन।
english: Ghee cooked with oil as a quarter, an anuvāsana that destroys Pitta.
notes: 'tailapāda' = having oil as one quarter (of the ghee, as is understood; the line does not say of what). No verb.

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (the drug kuṣṭha, costus, Saussurea costus; standard)
nicula (disputed: Barringtonia or a cane; not enriched)

hindi: सेंधा नमक, मदन, कुष्ठ नामक औषध यानी कूठ, शताह्वा यानी सोआ, निचुल और वचा।
english: Rock salt (saindhava), madana, kuṣṭha (the drug costus), śatāhvā (dill), nicula and vacā (sweet flag),

text_flags.why: possible: 'nicala' (motionless) is not a drug name here; 'nicula' is a known drug (Barringtonia acutangula or a cane) and fits a list of drugs

notes: List in the nominative (neuter nominative equals accusative). 'nicala' vs 'nicula' is doubtful, so no identification is added; nicula is disputed (Barringtonia acutangula, hijjala, or Calamus, vetasa). Here kuṣṭha is the drug, not the skin disease; costus (Saussurea costus) is standard.

words.gloss: together with; kaṭphala (box myrtle, Myrica esculenta; standard)

hindi: ह्रीबेर यानी सुगन्धबाला, मधुक, भार्गी, देवदार और कायफल सहित।
english: Hrīvera (Pavonia odorata), madhuka, bhārgī, devadāru (deodar cedar), together with kaṭphala (Myrica esculenta).
notes: Orthographic: printed 'hrībera' (ba for va), normalised to hrīvera. hrīvera = Pavonia odorata (standard; often given as balā-type fragrant root); devadāru = Cedrus deodara (standard); kaṭphala = Myrica esculenta (standard). 'sakaṭphalam' is 'with kaṭphala'.

words.gloss: puṣkara (probably puṣkaramūla, Inula racemosa; probable, the lotus is also meant by the word)

hindi: नागर यानी सोंठ, पुष्कर यानी सम्भवतः पुष्करमूल, मेदा, चविका यानी सम्भवतः चव्य, चित्रक यानी चीता और शठी।
english: Nāgara (dry ginger), puṣkara (probably puṣkaramūla, Inula racemosa), medā, cavikā (probably Piper chaba), citraka (Plumbago zeylanica) and śaṭhī.
notes: List in the nominative. nāgara = dried ginger (standard); puṣkara = puṣkaramūla, Inula racemosa (probable; it is also a word for lotus); cavikā = Piper chaba/retrofractum (probable); citraka = Plumbago zeylanica (standard).

words.gloss: viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes; standard); ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum; standard)
śyāmā (disputed: black turpeth or another plant; not enriched)
hareṇu (disputed, a seed drug; not enriched)

hindi: विडंग और अतिविषा यानी अतीस, श्यामा, हरेणु, नीलिनी यानी नील और स्थिरा यानी सम्भवतः शालपर्णी।
english: Viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes) and ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum), śyāmā, hareṇu, nīlinī (indigo) and sthirā (probably śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum),
notes: 'viḍaṅgātiviṣe' is read as a dual dvandva 'viḍaṅga and ativiṣā'. Identifications: viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard); ativiṣā = Aconitum heterophyllum (standard); śyāmā = disputed (trivṛt variety, Ichnocarpus and others); hareṇu = disputed (renukā, seeds of Vitex or Piper species); nīlinī = Indigofera tinctoria (standard); sthirā = śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum (probable). The word viḍa (salt) of the glossary is not used here.

words.gloss: bilva (see unit 100); ajamodā (probably Trachyspermum roxburghianum, celery-seed type; probable)
capalā (a name of pippalī, long pepper, in some lists; disputed)

hindi: बिल्व और अजमोदा यानी सम्भवतः अजमोद, चपला, दन्ती यानी जंगली जमालगोटा और रास्ना, उन समान भागों वालों के साथ।
english: Bilva and ajamodā (probably celery-seed type, Trachyspermum roxburghianum), capalā, dantī (Baliospermum montanum) and rāsnā, with those, equal (ones).
notes: 'taiḥ samaiḥ' = with those, equal (ones): the sense is probably 'in equal parts', but 'parts' is not in the Sanskrit. 'bilvājamode' read as a dual dvandva. capalā: in some lists a name of pippalī; disputed, so left unenriched in the translation. ajamodā = Trachyspermum roxburghianum (probable). dantī = Baliospermum montanum (standard).

words.gloss: Kapha; disease; removing (final d written t)

hindi: एरण्ड का तेल यानी अरंडी का तेल तैयार किया जाए, या तेल; कफ के रोगों को दूर करने वाला।
english: Castor oil (airaṇḍa-taila) is to be prepared, or oil, removing diseases of Kapha.
notes: Read as 'castor oil is to be prepared (cooked), or (another) oil'; with what it is cooked is not said (the ingredients of the preceding units). 'kapharoga' = disease of Kapha. airaṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard; also noted in unit 93).

words.gloss: vardhma (scrotal swelling, probably hernia or hydrocele; probable)
udāvarta (reversal of the downward movement of wind and wastes; standard)

hindi: वर्ध्म यानी अण्डवृद्धि, उदावर्त, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, अर्श यानी बवासीर, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली का रोग और मेह यानी मूत्र के रोग, वात सहित।
english: Vardhma, udāvarta, gulma, arśas (haemorrhoids), plīha and meha (urinary disorders), together with wind (māruta),
notes: The accusative objects; their verb 'hanyāt' stands in the next unit. Orthographic: printed 'udāvartta' written udāvarta. Identifications: arśas = haemorrhoids (standard); vardhma = enlargement of the scrotum, hernia or hydrocele (probable); udāvarta = upward movement of wind (standard); gulma = abdominal lump (standard); plīha = disorder of the spleen (standard); meha = the group of urinary disorders (prameha); whether diabetes is included is not settled here. 'samārutān' = 'together with māruta (wind)'.

words.gloss: ānāha (distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind)

hindi: आनाह यानी पेट का फूलना और मल-वायु का रुकना, और अश्मरी यानी पथरी, इन्हें वह अनुवासन शीघ्र नष्ट कर दे।
english: That anuvāsana would quickly destroy ānāha (distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind) and aśmarī (urinary stone).
notes: Continues the sentence of the previous unit: 'hanyāt' takes the accusatives listed in the unit before. 'anuvāsana' see unit 98. aśmarī = urinary calculus (standard); ānāha = distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind (standard).
